question:
A 52-year-old woman with diabetes reports experiencing pain and tingling in her left arm, specifically on
the ulnar side of her hand and wrist. She denies any weakness or difficulty with fine motor skills. Her
symptoms worsen when she sleeps on her left side without a pillow and with her left elbow extended,
but improve when she sleeps with her left hand elevated above her head. What is the most likely

diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Myofascial pain syndrome (B) Peripheral neuropathy due to diabetes
(C) Radial nerve compression (D) Median nerve entrapment at the wrist (E) Guyon’s canal syndrome
(F) Brachial plexopathy (G) Cervical radiculopathy (H) Ulnar nerve entrapment at the elbow (I) Cubital
tunnel syndrome (J) Carpal tunnel syndrome
 A. Brachial plexopathy
B. Carpal tunnel syndrome
C. Peripheral neuropathy due to diabetes
D. Guyon’s canal syndrome
E. Radial nerve compression
F. Median nerve entrapment at the wrist
G. Cubital tunnel syndrome
H. Cervical radiculopathy
I. Myofascial pain syndrome
J. Ulnar nerve entrapment at the elbow
